summary: Decouple the scaffold-report schema's build_type from a fixed enum so the scaffold phase is genuinely dir-driven: any template folder under templates/ that a project references should render AND have its scaffold-report.json validate, mirroring the slug pattern the requirements schema already uses.
goals: Make scaffold-report.schema.json accept any lowercase build_type slug instead of the fixed [game, cli, app, library, other] enum.
Keep the scaffold-report build_type validation aligned with requirements.schema.json so the two never drift.
Remove the last place where adding a new template requires editing a hardcoded list, fulfilling the dir-driven one-folder promise.
Prove the decoupling with a regression test that scaffolds a novel build_type and asserts its report validates.

features.name: Slug-pattern build_type in scaffold-report schema
features.description: Replace the build_type enum in contracts/schemas/v1/scaffold-report.schema.json with { type: string, pattern: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]* } matching requirements.schema.json.

features.name: Enum-free scaffold error message
features.description: Update the missing-build_type error in cli/lib/scaffold.js so it no longer hardcodes (game|cli|app|library|other); point the operator at templates/ instead.

features.name: Novel-build_type regression test
features.description: Add a test that renders a build_type with no entry in the old enum and asserts both scaffold success and scaffold-report validation pass.

constraints: No LLM anywhere in the CLI; this is a deterministic schema/validation change.
Zero new dependencies; reuse the existing custom validator and scaffold pipeline.
Do not change build-manifest or build-report schemas (already enum-free) or any other phase.
Test-first: add the failing regression test before changing the schema.
Single task touching tests/appbuilder.test.js — no overlapping concurrent tasks.
